content:
Wen Jiabao, Jia Qinglin and others attend the conference

A ceremony marking the 100th anniversary of Jiang Zemin's birth was held at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing on Monday (17th). Xi Jinping, General Secretary of the CPC Central Committee, President of the State, and Chairman of the Central Military Commission, as well as all current members of the Politburo Standing Committee, attended. Retired leaders including Wen Jiabao, Jia Qinglin, Zhang Dejiang, Yu Zhengsheng, Li Zhanshu, Wang Yang, Li Lanqing, Zeng Qinghong, Li Changchun, He Guoqiang, Liu Yunshan, Wang Qishan, and Zhang Gaoli also attended the ceremony.

Hu Jintao not seen; Li Ruihuan, Wu Guanzheng and Luo Gan absent

However, Hu Jintao, who succeeded Jiang Zemin as General Secretary of the CPC Central Committee, President of the State, and Chairman of the Central Military Commission, was not seen in CCTV's live broadcast. In addition, Li Ruihuan, Wu Guanzheng, and Luo Gan, who had served as members of the Politburo Standing Committee during Jiang's era, also missed the ceremony.

"The serious political disturbances of 1989: Jiang firmly implemented the CPC Central Committee's decisions"

Xi Jinping delivered an important speech at the ceremony. Recounting how Jiang Zemin rose from Shanghai Party Secretary to the core of the third generation of the CPC central leadership, he particularly noted: "In the spring and summer of 1989, serious political disturbances occurred in our country. Comrade Jiang Zemin firmly upheld and implemented the correct decisions of the CPC Central Committee, and effectively maintained stability in Shanghai."

Xi Jinping also said that people should learn from Jiang Zemin's "unwavering political faith". He described how, amid the major tests of changing international circumstances in the late 1980s and early 1990s and the serious political disturbances at home, Jiang remained firm in prioritising economic development. He also emphasised the importance of governing the country first by governing the Party, and of governing the Party strictly.

Xi Jinping also said that people should learn from Jiang Zemin's "farsighted strategic thinking". He mentioned Jiang's leadership in achieving the smooth return of Hong Kong and Macao, as well as promoting the "1992 Consensus" between the two sides of the Taiwan Strait, which embodies the One-China principle.

The outside world is focused on the political signals sent by Beijing's decision to hold a major event for Jiang Zemin's centenary at this time and by Xi's speech.

Chen Daoyin, an independent political scholar, said that holding major commemorative events for the centenary of a deceased leader is an institutional convention. Many important leaders in the past, including Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping, were also commemorated with major events marking their centenaries. As the core of the third generation of the CPC central leadership, Jiang's centenary being marked by a major commemorative event is consistent with established practice and protocol.

Scholar: 1989 wording contains no new formulation

Regarding Xi's active discussion of Jiang's political position in 1989 while commemorating him, Chen Daoyin believes that 1989 was an important turning point in both Chinese politics and Jiang's political career. That year, because he "took the right side", Jiang, then a local leader nearing retirement, was appointed to replace Zhao Ziyang in Beijing amid the crisis, becoming the core of the third generation of the CPC central leadership. Therefore, any review of his life must address the events of 1989.

Chen Daoyin said that Jiang's firm support for the decisions of the CPC Central Committee at the time echoed Xi's current political requirement to uphold the authority of the Central Committee and the core position of the General Secretary, making it even more necessary to raise the matter again. He also believed that Xi's remarks concerning 1989 amounted to a final, definitive assessment and did not introduce a new formulation. There is therefore no need for the outside world to over-interpret Xi's renewed mention of 1989.

Jiang's centenary was marked by a major commemorative event, but Hu Jintao, the core of the fourth generation of the CPC central leadership, was absent. Chen Daoyin said that although retired leaders are not necessarily required to attend such events, as Jiang's successor, Hu would normally have been expected to attend a major event commemorating Jiang. His absence may have been due to the fact that he was not in Beijing, was unwell, or for other reasons. Chen noted that attention could be paid to whether Hu sent a wreath to Zhu Rongji's funeral on Tuesday (18th).

Zhao Jianmin, former dean of the College of Social Sciences at Chinese Culture University in Taiwan and a specialist in China's political development and cross-Strait relations, believes that Xi's speech provided a comprehensive review of Jiang's life. Several key aspects of Jiang's political career, including the introduction of the important thought of the "Three Represents", the cross-Strait "1992 Consensus", and his firm support for the decisions of the CPC Central Committee in 1989, are indispensable to any account of him.

Zhao Jianmin said it was normal for Xi to discuss only Jiang's firm stance in support of the CPC Central Committee in 1989, without elaborating further on the Tiananmen Square incident.

Zhao Jianmin also pointed out that Xi's emphasis on Jiang's centenary had personal factors. He believes that Xi's later advancement—from a leader in Fujian who was successively transferred to Zhejiang and Shanghai, major economic provinces in China, to serve as the top official—laid the foundation for his entry into the highest level of leadership, and that Jiang played an important and crucial role in this process.

He believes that Xi's emphasis on commemorative events for Jiang shows, on the one hand, that Xi values old ties and is grateful. On the other hand, Xi's assessment of Jiang, with its emphasis on his promotion of strict Party governance and anti-corruption efforts, can also demonstrate that the relevant policies inherit and continue the direction of work from Jiang's era. It is the implementation of an existing consensus within the Party and can help clarify rumours circulating among the public.

Highlighting the importance of obeying the CPC Central Committee at moments involving major matters of principle

However, veteran China political commentator Cai Shenkun holds a different view. He described Xi's public mention of Jiang's position during the 1989 "political disturbances" as unusual, and said that both Jiang while he was alive and his family after his death had wanted to downplay, rather than emphasise, how he rose to the highest centre of power as a result of the Tiananmen Square incident.

Cai Shenkun believes that Xi's special emphasis on this point on this occasion was intended to highlight the importance of obeying the CPC Central Committee and maintaining political loyalty at moments involving major matters of principle.

Cai also pointed out that the 21st National Congress of the Communist Party of China—referred to as the "CPC 21st National Congress"—is expected to convene next autumn. He believes that Xi's emphasis on Jiang's centenary, as well as his praise for Jiang's choice to firmly uphold the CPC Central Committee, serves on the one hand to emphasise the political succession relationship between himself and Jiang and strengthen recognition of the continuity of his politics. On the other hand, commemorating Jiang also allows him to reiterate to Party members the importance of obeying the Central Committee and maintaining political loyalty.
